about: The Bible maps shipped in the app (Map > Bible maps). Same folder and file for the phone. Credits must be shown with each map.

rand-mcnally-1910.name: Rand McNally, 1910
rand-mcnally-1910.text: Rand McNally, “The modern world and the Bible lands”, 1910. Public domain. From Project Gutenberg, through Wikimedia Commons. Shown at a smaller file size, otherwise unchanged.

rawson-1873.name: A. L. Rawson, 1873
rawson-1873.text: The plan of Jerusalem from A. L. Rawson, “Map of Palestine and all Bible lands” (H. H. Lloyd & Co., 1873). Public domain. Scan by the Norman B. Leventhal Map Center at the Boston Public Library, through Wikimedia Commons. Shown at a smaller file size, otherwise unchanged.

maps.title: The twelve tribes of Israel
maps.description: Where each tribe settled in the land after the conquest, with the cities of refuge marked.

passages.label: Joshua 13: the lands of the tribes

maps.title: The kingdoms of Saul, David and Solomon
maps.description: How far the kingdom reached under Saul, then under David and Solomon, and the lands beyond it that Solomon controlled.

passages.label: 2 Samuel 5: David reigns over all Israel
1 Kings 4:21: the extent of Solomon's rule

maps.title: The kingdoms of Israel and Judah
maps.description: The land after the kingdom divided: Israel in the north and east, Judah in the south, with the cities named in the books of Kings.

maps.title: The ministry of Jesus
maps.description: Where Jesus went, with a note on what the Gospels tell of each place and the main roads. A question mark before a name means the place is uncertain.

maps.title: Christ in Judea
maps.description: Judea, Samaria and the Jordan valley: the cities named in the Gospels, other towns of the time, and places whose site is uncertain.

maps.title: Plan of Jerusalem, 1873
maps.description: A nineteenth-century plan of Jerusalem and its surroundings: the temple hill (Moriah), Zion, the Mount of Olives, and the Kidron, Hinnom and Siloam valleys. It marks the holy places as they were understood in 1873, and many of those sites are traditional, not certain.

maps.title: Paul's journeys
maps.description: Paul's first, second and third journeys and his voyage to Rome, with the outer limit of Roman rule.

maps.title: The places in Corinthians
maps.description: The cities and regions named in 1 and 2 Corinthians: Corinth in Achaia, Ephesus, Macedonia, Troas, Galatia, Asia, Damascus and Judea.

maps.title: The modern world and the Bible lands (1910)
maps.description: A world map of 1910 with the lands of the Bible marked inside the red lines; the names and borders of the world are those of 1910.

passages.label: Acts 1:8: to the ends of the earth
